add.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia)
add.summary: Fetched (HTTP 200, cached). Article's Brazil content documents only the right to same-sex-partner conjugal visitations in all Brazilian jails from February 2015, per the National Criminal and Penitentiary Council; it contains no Bahia-specific trans-prisoner placement rule, special unit, segregation practice, or documented case. A later passing 'Bahia' mention in the same article's sourcing relates to a Salvador City Council candidate, not prison housing.

add.title: LGBTQ rights in Brazil (Wikipedia)
add.summary: Fetched (HTTP 200, cached). Documents the national framework governing trans prisoners that applies uniformly across Brazilian states including Bahia: LGBTQ people have a special, separate place in Brazilian prisons; transsexuals have the right to be addressed by their social name rather than birth name; to be forwarded to women's prisons (i.e. placement by gender identity); and to choose male or female clothing. No state-level/state-DOC (Secretaria de Administração Penitenciária da Bahia) placement detail is given.
